findings.quote: "Your family relies on your strength, and few of them know what it cost you to build."
findings.issue: The last sentence of How you are has no "you" as its subject, against the voice law.
findings.fix: "At home you protect your family closely, and you take on their problems before they ask. Because you learned early to carry weight without help, you find it hard to let anyone see you struggle. Your family relies on your strength, and you have told few of them what it cost you to build."

findings.quote: "Your family feels secure with you, and some of them wish you were less strict."
findings.issue: The last sentence of How you are has no "you" as its subject.
findings.fix: "You run your household on clear duties and fair rules, and the people in it know what to expect. Because order is how you protect the people you love, you notice a broken promise at home faster than a kind word. Your family feels secure with you, and you know some of them wish you were less strict."

findings.quote: "Your family depends on that order, and they know less of your heart than of your plans."
findings.issue: The last sentence of How you are has no "you" as its subject.
findings.fix: "You look after your family by keeping everything in order, the papers sorted and the promises kept. Because reliability is how you express love, you are more at ease arranging things for people than talking about feelings. Your family depends on that order, and you show them less of your heart than of your plans."

findings.quote: "Since your mid-thirties you have put work and your own direction before family life, and relatives have seen less of you than they wanted."
findings.issue: It reads a definite neglect from an empty seat (the Day pillar is the self and partner palace, 三命通会 卷二, and an empty seat says nothing about neglect). On D023 the reader is still 34 (M-6), so the span covers nothing.
findings.fix: "Your Home Chapter seats no character over family, so since your mid-thirties you have run your family life on what your earlier gates set."

findings.quote: "often an adult who lived in their own head"
findings.issue: "Often" is a banned hedge.
findings.fix: "In your first home an adult who lived in their own head gave you books, questions or long silences in place of the usual fuss. By your teens you had learned to answer your own questions, and you asked for help less than other children did."

findings.quote: "often an older relative who gave without being asked"
findings.issue: "Often" is a banned hedge.
findings.fix: "Someone in your early life, an older relative who gave without being asked, made comfort a daily thing. You still judge a home by how it feels to walk into, and you have made yours warmer than the ones you grew up beside."

findings.quote: "you came through on a family that forgave more than you expected"
findings.issue: "Came through on" is a broken idiom.
findings.fix: "Plans and people far from home pulled you away in those years, and your family saw less of you than they wanted. You made it up in bursts of generosity, and you came through because your family forgave more than you expected."

findings.quote: "your best days in those years have been reunions"
findings.issue: "Those years" puts in the past the gate the reader is still living in (48 on, now).
findings.fix: "Your family has scattered across more than one place since your late forties, and the younger ones live far from you and from each other. You have become the one who brings them together, and your best days in these years have been reunions."

findings.quote: "Because a well kept home"
findings.issue: A compound adjective before its noun takes a hyphen (the corpus already writes "strong-willed" and "mid-thirties").
findings.fix: "You keep your household running, the cupboards full and the bills paid before they are due. Because a well-kept home is how you show love, you feel uneasy when things at home are left undone. Your family feels safe without knowing how much you do, and you rarely tell them."

findings.quote: "built on structure, regular meals and shared duties and arrangements that hold … the one who keeps its promises when others forgot"
findings.issue: The list misparses on first read, and "keeps" clashes in tense with "forgot".
findings.fix: "Your family life has been built on structure, with regular meals, shared duties and arrangements that hold. Relatives on both sides have come to trust your household, and you have been the one who kept its promises when others forgot."

findings.quote: "Keeping the household in order … The order you built keeps you going"
findings.issue: "Order" comes twice in two short sentences.
findings.fix: "Keeping the household in order weighs on you in these years, and you carry more of it than your share. The routines you built keep you going, and you pass some of the load over once your family sees it."

findings.quote: "the care came with expectations. You kept the peace by doing what was expected"
findings.issue: "Expectations" and "expected" clash across two adjacent sentences.
findings.fix: "Your family sheltered you in those years more than you needed, and the care came with expectations. You kept the peace by doing as you were asked, and what carried you was one thing you chose for yourself."

findings.pages: D143, D157, D177, D181, D182, D186, D189, D192 (and the 14 younger pages, where it is harmless)
findings.quote: "An older relative takes a closer interest in your home this year"
findings.issue: For readers aged 63 to 68 an older relative stepping in is rarely true. A Sage year is support received from any side (渊海子平 论印绶: 印 brings shelter, 庇荫), and Y1 allows one line for all ages.
findings.fix: "A relative takes a closer interest in your home this year with help and opinions, and you are looked after more than you asked to be."

findings.quote: "you feel its pull long after you have left home"
findings.issue: It asserts the reader has left home, which the chart cannot know (D130 is 26). The Year seat reads the family of origin (渊海子平 年为祖上), not where the reader lives.
findings.fix: "The expectations you grew up with stay with you, and you feel uneasy when a family duty goes undone. Because approval at home came through doing things right, you check yourself against what your elders would think. Your bond with your family is strong and dutiful, and you feel its pull wherever you live."

findings.quote: "Two seats rule Family in your chart. Two sit in your Early Chapter."
findings.issue: When every seat sits in one chapter, the second count repeats the first.
findings.fix: When all seats share one chapter: "{N} seats rule {Domain} in your chart. Both sit in your {Chapter}." (two seats) · "{N} seats rule {Domain} in your chart. All {n} sit in your {Chapter}." (three or more) · "One seat rules {Domain} in your chart. It sits in your {Chapter}." (one seat).

findings.quote: "Add your birth hour to read your late chapter."
findings.issue: "Late Chapter" is a chapter name, capitalised in every label. The no-seat variant of the same note ("Your Hour Gate may hold a {d} seat.") carries the banned hedge "may".
findings.fix: Seats shown: "Your Hour Gate is closed. Add your birth hour to read your Late Chapter." No seat: "Your Hour Gate can hold a {d} seat. Add your birth hour to read your Late Chapter."

findings.quote: recognition "you say yes before you read the terms" / lived "by saying yes before you had read the terms" (piancai_day_branch, D026); recognition "you avoid risks that would make you rich quickly" / lived "You have turned down at least one exciting offer because it asked too much risk" (zhengcai_month_branch, D028, D069, D187); recognition "write down too little of it" / lived "more than once without noting to whom" (piancai_hour_stem, D172)
findings.issue: When the lead seat's gate is open, How you are and that seat's lived beat tell the reader the same pattern twice, often with the same nouns, so step 2 adds nothing to step 1.
findings.fix: **Rule.** A seat's lived beat names a past turn or a consequence that its recognition leaves out. It shares no scene noun and no act with the recognition: the gate fails a shared four-word run or two shared content nouns between a seat's `.recognition` and `.lived`. Then rewrite the eight lived beats above. Fallback in the resolver: when the lead seat's gate is the reader's current gate, its lived beat is shown only under "the pattern so far" and is held back from step 2 if it fails that check. **Evidence:** 8 of the 16 distinct Wealth lead seats that show both parts on a page, on 13 of 28 Wealth pages. The 20 Love pages show that the rule can be met: their lived beats name a past act the recognition does not ("over who apologised first", "you had forgotten how to do it yourself").

findings.quote: "Careful earning paid off in those years, and you saved steadily from regular work." (D114, ages 6 to 15); "Openings came your way in those years … and you grew bolder with it." (D072, ages 1 to 10); "Expenses felt heavy in those years, and you counted money long after there was enough." (D091, ages 1 to 10)
findings.issue: The six lived Wealth decade lines are written for an earning adult, and the resolver shows the last past decade even when it fell in childhood, so a toddler "counted money" and a child "saved steadily from regular work".
findings.fix: **Rule.** A lived decade that ends before sixteen is not read as the reader's own earning. Either step 2 skips it in Wealth, Career and Love, or it reads from a new unit, `decade_lines.<Domain>.<pole>.early`, written in the family's frame ("Money at home …", "You grew up while …"). For Wealth that is 6 new units (Rival, Horizon and Steward, helping and heavy). **Classical:** 三命通会 (论小运) and 渊海子平 (童限) read the childhood years through the small luck and the parents' house, not as the child's own fortune. The brief's own law agrees: "An Early Chapter lived beat fits a child." **Evidence:** 8 of 28 Wealth pages have a decade wholly or mostly before sixteen, and 2 more start one in the early teens.

findings.pages: D135 on the page; D999 raw
findings.quote: To a 24-year-old: "You notice a chance to earn where others see an ending, a late venture or a deal offered by someone younger." Raw: "In later life you move toward advisory work", "You stay in demand late", "You grow in later life through two or three people"
findings.issue: When no seat's gate has opened, `domainsResolve.js` line 82 falls back to the highest-ranked seat of all, so an Hour seat's recognition becomes How you are for a reader under 48, and eight of these recognitions describe later life as the reader's present.
findings.fix: **Rule.** Every Hour-seat recognition reads true at any age. It names the drive, and later life moves into the ahead beat, as `zhengcai_hour_stem` and `zhengcai_hour_branch` already do (D041 at 34 and D122 at 28 read correctly). Or, as a resolver rule: when no gate has opened, How you are shows `domain_unruled.<Domain>` and the Hour seat appears only as an ahead beat. Rewrites for the two on-page and nearest units are DB-014 and DB-017. **Evidence:** 1 page in this sample and 7 raw recognitions in D999, 8 units in all. Reach is low, because those are the units no sampled chart reached, but the misfire is certain when they do show.

findings.pages: D091, D103, D126, D165, D180, D187 (every page where it fires; all six are Underfueled)
findings.quote: "what you make turns into money more easily for you than for most"
findings.issue: The pairing fires on presence alone (`domainsResolve.js` step 1; `tgPatterns.js` has no strength condition), and on these pages it lands only on Underfueled charts, so the line reads as a gift where the classics read output feeding wealth as a drain on a core already short.
findings.fix: **Rule.** 食伤生财 fires as written only on Overfueled and Balanced charts. On an Underfueled chart it either stays silent or reads from a weak-chart line, for example: "What you make turns into money readily, and each season of earning takes more out of you than it pays back." **Classical:** 子平真诠 论食神, "食神生财，美格也……如身强食旺而财透，大贵之格": the pairing is good on a strong body. On a weak one, output and wealth both draw on the self (泄耗交加; 渊海子平 财多身弱，富屋贫人). The heavy Steward and Horizon decades on the same six pages read the chart the classical way, so the pair line also stands against them. 比劫夺财's line is two-sided ("you also find your safety net among those same people") and holds on both bands. **Evidence:** 6 of 6 pages in this group. Check the other strength-bound pairings (财官相生, 官印相生) and the Blueprint's part 4, which triggers on the same table.

findings.pages: all 49; worst D028, D072, D114, D180, D187 (14 to 16 each)
findings.quote: "… , and you relax a little each time you check." · "… , and you come through with your savings intact." · "… , and you decide how much of your own you put in." (all three on D008, with 8 more "and you" joints)
findings.issue: The easiest way to pass the gate's reader-last test is ", and you …", so 108 of the 156 distinct non-headline units on these pages close on that joint, and a Wealth page carries it 2 to 16 times.
findings.fix: **Rule.** The gate accepts the reader-last close in any shape (a "You …" sentence, "What you …", a clause led by you after "because" or "since") and caps the ", and you" close at one unit in three within each file (a character's decade lines, a seat's four parts). The page check fails a Domains page with more than four. **Evidence:** 108 of 156 units (69%). Compound check "joint 'and you'": 8 or more on 19 of 28 Wealth pages (seat cards included), 2 to 5 on the shorter Love pages.

findings.criterion: A1 (no claim the chart cannot know)
findings.pages: D033, D042, D047, D055, D065, D088, D098, D104, D119, D125 (every Love page for a reader under 35)
findings.quote: "From your mid-thirties your love life settles into a shared home with a partner" (shishen); "a shared home and a shared name for what you are" (zhengguan); "From your mid-thirties you share a home with a partner as bold as you are" (jiecai); "You build a home in these years with someone" (piancai)
findings.issue: All ten Love ahead beats state as fact that a shared home with a partner arrives at 35, though the Day seat shows only what kind of bond the reader makes and the page has no Love decade to time it.
findings.fix: **Rule.** A Love ahead beat says how love runs for the reader in these years: what they look for, and how a bond with a partner goes. It sets the partner in a general or conditional frame ("a partner", "with a partner in these years") and never announces a home or a marriage. This keeps Q10 ("a partner" at the Day Gate) and does not re-open it. Example for shishen: "From your mid-thirties love for you settles around ordinary days made pleasant, the shared table and the quiet evening. With a partner in these years you are looked after in return more than at any time before." **Classical:** 三命通会 (论夫妻, 论妻妾) and 渊海子平 read the spouse's nature from the day branch, and the timing of a marriage from the decades and years that meet the spouse star or palace. Primer §10: never assert a guaranteed outcome. **Evidence:** 10 of 10 Love ahead units, on 10 of 20 Love pages. The TWEAKs DB-035 and DB-036 fix only grammar in two of these units and are interim until the rule is applied.

findings.quote: "your income has stayed below what you could earn" beside "Careful earning paid off in those years" (D051), "most of them pay" (Horizon decade now: D051, D063, D080) and "Money reached you by routes regular pay never took" (D114)
findings.issue: The gap row claims an income outcome for the whole Rising Chapter, while a helping Wealth decade on the same page says the money came in those same years.
findings.fix: Rewrite: "Since sixteen you have put work, study and friends before money, and your income has followed your decades more than any plan of your own." (25 words; it agrees with the NOTE "your decades set its course"). **Classical:** 子平真诠 论行运: the decade supplies what the chart's seats do not, so where no seat rules wealth, the decade sets the outcome.

findings.quote: "You have kept to your own plan while friends chased quick gains" beside the Rival's "More than once you lent or spent a windfall on friends within weeks" (D072); "the savings finally visible" beside "has gone into travel, new projects and the plans of younger people more than into reserves" (D180)
findings.issue: Two seats of opposite characters share a gate, and each lived beat holds a comparison ("while friends chased", "more than into reserves") that denies the other seat.
findings.fix: Rewrite zhengcai_month_stem.lived: "The money you have counted on since your late teens is the salary, raised a step at a time and planned for well in advance. You have kept to your own plan through lean months and good ones, and you have rarely regretted it." Rewrite piancai_hour_branch.lived: "Your money since your late forties has gone into travel, new projects and the plans of younger people. You have earned well from at least one late venture, and you have spent a good part of it on getting people together." Writing rule for lived beats: no comparison against another character's behaviour. **Classical:** 子平真诠 论用神 (透干 and 藏支): the revealed stem and the hidden branch of one pillar are two sides of the same gate, not two verdicts.

findings.pages: D072, D105 (against the Horizon on D017, D091, D105)
findings.quote: Rival "Your money comes in bursts, and leaves with friends." / Horizon "Your money arrives in windfalls and leaves through friends." (D091). Rival "More than once you lent or spent a windfall on friends within weeks" / Horizon "More than once you have spent a windfall on friends and new plans" (both on D105)
findings.issue: The Rival's Month units carry the Horizon's windfall and its generosity, so on D105 two characters say one thing in one gate.
findings.fix: Headline: "You earn hardest when someone is racing you." Recognition: "You earn in step with the people around you, chasing the same bonus or backing the same venture as your friends. Because keeping up is how you show you belong, you match their spending before you count your own. You save less than you mean to in the good years as well as the lean ones, and you feel it most after a win." Lived: "Your income since your late teens has risen and dipped with the people you measure yourself against, the friend's venture joined or the bonus chased. More than once you spent a win on keeping pace with them, and you counted it as the price of staying in the race." **Classical:** 渊海子平 论偏财: the Horizon is open-handed money that comes by the side door (慷慨, 横财). 三命通会 论劫财: the Rival contests money with peers (争夺, 破耗). House portrait (05 §5): "comparison as fuel; the race".

findings.pages: D114, D118 (against the Horizon Year stem on D072, D080)
findings.quote: "money that comes in through friends or luck goes out the same way" (banned "luck"); "Money arrived and vanished in your family … You had your own share of that nerve" (nothing for "that nerve" to point back to); compare the Horizon's "As a child you watched money arrive in good months and go out"
findings.issue: The early Rival reads as the early Horizon (money arriving and leaving), and the units also carry a banned word and a dangling "that nerve".
findings.fix: Recognition: "You spend quickly and in company, and money that comes in through friends goes out keeping up with them. Because a free hand with money was admired at home when you were young, saving feels cautious to you in a way you dislike. Your bank balance swings more than most people's, and you are calm about it until a lean month arrives." Lived: "Money in your family moved fast while you were growing up, won boldly and gone again on keeping up with others. You were as daring with money as your family before you were grown, and you spent what you had almost as soon as you had it." **Classical:** as DB-009 (三命通会 论劫财).

findings.pages: D065, D195 (against the General on D104, D161 and the Twin on D033, D148)
findings.quote: Rival "You fall for people who push back." / General "You love people strong enough to push back." Rival "Partners with a temper, an opinion and plans of their own" / Twin "people with their own opinions and their own plans"
findings.issue: The Rival's Love units read as the General's force and the Twin's equality, and none of them shows the Rival's own contest over pride and money that its seat card names.
findings.fix: Headline: "You love the people you can race." Recognition: "You fall for partners who compete with you, in pride, in plans and over money. Because keeping pace with someone is how you know you matter to them, a calm and agreeable partner bores you within months. You keep loving through the contests, and you count a quiet week as a sign that something has gone wrong." **Classical:** 三命通会 (论妻妾): the Rival in the spouse seat brings rivalry and money contested inside the marriage (夫妻争财), while the General in the spouse seat brings a forceful, pressing partner (七杀坐日支).

findings.quote: "a meal ready or a problem fixed" (the Artisan's "the meal made"); "Because reliability is what made you feel loved" (the Magistrate's "Because reliability is what love means to you"); "people who turned up on time and kept their word" (the Sage's "the partner who turns up on time", the Magistrate's "people who keep their word"); "before your partner mentions it"
findings.issue: The Steward's Love units are made of three neighbours' lines, the Artisan, the Magistrate and the Sage, and the recognition assumes the reader has a partner now.
findings.fix: Recognition: "You show love by providing, the rent covered and the house kept running before a partner thinks to ask. Because a well-kept home is how you feel safe, you trust a partner who looks after shared things as carefully as you do. You let romance fade when the upkeep fills every evening." Lived: "The partners who have lasted with you so far cared about upkeep and careful money as much as you did. More than once you have kept a shared home running so well that you noticed the quiet in the romance only afterwards." **Classical:** 三命通会 (论妻妾): the Steward in the spouse seat is provision and a well-kept house (正财坐日支, 持家), the "slow ledger" of the house portrait (05 §5).

findings.quote: General "Your family measures itself against your standards." / Magistrate "Your family takes its standards from you." General "you notice the slip before the effort" / Magistrate "you notice when someone falls short of it". Last sentence "Your family respects you deeply, and some of them wait a long time for your praise."
findings.issue: The General and the Magistrate at the Hour Gate read as one force (standards and withheld praise), and the General's last sentence has the family, not the reader, as its subject.
findings.fix: Headline: "Your family learns to rise to your pressure." Recognition: "You push the younger people in your family hard, and you hand them the tests you once passed yourself. Because pressure is how you show belief in someone, the people close to you feel the weight before they feel the care. You earn your family's respect through the hard years, and you make some of them wait a long time for your praise." **Classical:** 子平真诠 论偏官: the General is the force that presses on the self and forges it. 论正官: the Magistrate is the rule that orders.

findings.quote: General "the one called when a problem is too hard for anyone else" / Alchemist "the expert called in when the usual answers run out", "You are hired for the problems nobody else can solve."
findings.issue: The General's later career reads as the Alchemist's rare knowledge, not as pressure, and it is tied to later life (DB-003).
findings.fix: Rewrite: "You are the one handed the crisis and the deadline nobody else will carry. Because pressure is where you feel useful, you take on more responsibility each year while people around you ease off. What you find hardest is a calendar with nothing urgent in it, and you fill it fast." **Classical:** 渊海子平 论偏印: the Alchemist is the side-door learning (偏门之学). 子平真诠 论偏官: the General is the hard test.

findings.quote: Sage "Because steadiness is what you offer" / Steward "Because reliability is what you offer"
findings.issue: The Sage's cause is the Steward's trait in the Steward's sentence frame, when the Sage at work is the one senior people shelter and teach.
findings.fix: Rewrite: "You win roles through references, qualifications and the good word of those above you. Because you learn best under someone's wing, senior people take you on early, and you rarely have to sell yourself. You find open competition uncomfortable and do your best work where trust is already in place." **Classical:** 渊海子平 论印绶: the Sage is learning and the shelter of seniors (长上庇护).

findings.quote: "You judge a relative by whether they keep their word, and you say so when they do not."
findings.issue: The early Sage closes on the Magistrate's rule-keeping, not on the shelter it names in its first sentence.
findings.fix: Rewrite: "The steady, patient care you had early is the measure you hold family to, and you notice quickly when it is missing. Because your first home gave you shelter and someone to learn from, you trust family as the place to turn first. You go to a relative for comfort before you go to a friend, and you give the same back." **Classical:** 三命通会: a Sage in the Year pillar is the shelter of elders (祖荫).

findings.quote: "a late venture or a deal offered by someone younger" (to a reader of 24); "Your plans live in your head far longer than they live on paper."
findings.issue: The recognition is tied to later life (DB-003), and its last sentence has "your plans", not the reader, as its subject.
findings.fix: Rewrite: "You notice a chance to earn where others see an ending, a venture someone else gave up on or a deal nobody followed up. Because new money excites you more than kept money, you give generously and write down too little of it. You carry your plans in your head far longer than you put them on paper."

findings.quote: "you keep only what has both names written down"
findings.issue: The close has to be read twice, and it works as counsel by condition (put it in both names).
findings.fix: Rewrite: "From your mid-thirties your income starts to rise through the life you share with a partner, through a joint venture, a move or an opening from their side. You will earn more in these years than in all the years before, and you see the part with no clear owner slip away."

findings.quote: "your affairs stay clear only where you have put the details in writing"
findings.issue: It is counsel by condition that restates the recognition's "write down too little of it" (D135) and sits beside a second "written down" close on D114.
findings.fix: Rewrite: "From your late forties chances to earn keep arriving, through new projects and through people a generation younger who want you involved. You give a great deal in these years, and you lose track of whatever you leave unwritten."

findings.quote: "you aim your sharpest words at the world outside your door"; seat card beside it: "the sharpest of it lands on the person you care about most"
findings.issue: The ahead beat removes the Virtuoso's cost at home and contradicts the seat card on the same page.
findings.fix: Rewrite (it also meets the DB-006 rule): "From your mid-thirties your home fills with talk, and you look for a partner who matches you word for word. With a partner in these years you grow closer through what you argue about, and you learn which of your sharpest words to keep for the world outside your door." **Classical:** 三命通会 (论女命): the Virtuoso in the spouse seat is the sharp tongue at home (伤官坐夫宫).

findings.quote: "a lucky move"
findings.issue: "lucky" carries the banned "luck".
findings.fix: Money comes to you through openings in these years more than through regular pay, an offer or a sale or a well-timed move. You take more chances with money in this decade than you are used to, and most of them pay.

findings.quote: "a lucky move"
findings.issue: "lucky" carries the banned "luck".
findings.fix: Openings came your way in those years, a well-timed move or a chance offer or someone who knew someone. Money reached you by routes regular pay never took, and you grew bolder with it.

findings.quote: "without luck or risk"
findings.issue: Banned word.
findings.fix: Careful earning paid off in those years, and you saved steadily from regular work. You built up something solid without windfalls or risk, and you trusted your own counting more than any tip.

findings.quote: "each lucky stretch"
findings.issue: "lucky" carries the banned "luck".
findings.fix: You earn in bursts, a run of good months and a quiet stretch after. Because each good season makes you sure of the next, you spend the winnings on a new chance before you have kept any. You are richer in the middle of each strong stretch than after it.

findings.quote: "how your own luck runs"
findings.issue: Banned word.
findings.fix: What you have earned since your late teens has followed your instinct, with good runs and lean months in turn. At least once you have lost the gains of a good year by chasing a better one, and you have learned how your own winning streaks run.

findings.quote: "Your luck with money improves"
findings.issue: Banned word in a headline.
findings.fix: Your chances with money grow the further you go.

findings.quote: "more often than it should"
findings.issue: "should" is banned on these pages.
findings.fix: Caution about money tightens in these years, and spending on yourself feels wrong even when you can afford it. You have more put by than you feel you have, and you relax a little each time you check.

findings.quote: "Underneath, what you make"
findings.issue: "Underneath", a leftover of the retired reading's "runs underneath", sounds like a hidden placement, which a pattern unit must not claim and which D126 contradicts with its Steward "in plain view".
findings.fix: What you make turns into money more easily for you than for most, and you earn most from the work that feels like play.

findings.quote: "Debts close"
findings.issue: Debts are cleared, not closed (the seat's own lived beat says "the debts cleared").
findings.fix: Your late forties are when years of steady saving finally show. Debts clear and the accounts settle, and you become the one in your family who has enough.

findings.quote: "through a move … one part of it never moves"
findings.issue: "move" and "moves" in one unit, in two senses.
findings.fix: Chances to earn keep reaching you from your late forties, through younger people or through a move. Your money stays lively in these years, and you sleep best when one part of it is never touched.

findings.quote: "keep your own floor only where you set the number"
findings.issue: "Keep your own floor" is not a B1 idiom, and "the number" needs a second read.
findings.fix: Younger people start to make claims on your money from your late forties. You will give more than you planned each time, and you will keep your own share only where you set its size before anyone asks.

findings.quote: "when your partner wants something"
findings.issue: "Your partner" asserts that the reader has one now, where Q10 allows "a partner".
findings.fix: You treat money in a relationship as joint, and you give freely when a partner wants something. Because loyalty to the person beside you outweighs any careful plan, the shared accounts blur and the arguments arrive later. You stay calmest about money when your share and theirs are kept apart, and you seldom manage it.

findings.quote: "you notice a partner who only takes much later than your friends do"
findings.issue: "Much later" can attach to "takes", so the close has to be read twice.
findings.fix: You love by doing, the meal made and the evening kept free and the worry taken off someone's hands. Since giving comfort is how you feel close, you feel most loved by a partner who receives it gladly and gives some back. You give without keeping count, and you are the last of your friends to notice a partner who only takes.

findings.quote: "In love you fall for people who widen your life" (the headline is "You fall for people who widen your life.")
findings.issue: The recognition opens on the headline word for word.
findings.fix: In love you fall for the one with plans and friends and somewhere to be. Because range is what draws you, you lose interest within months in a partner who only offers closeness. What you want is someone who brings the world home, and you grow restless with anyone who shuts it out.

findings.quote: "the tally between you grows shorter, and you find you can lean"
findings.issue: A tally does not grow shorter, and "you can lean" is a capacity close.
findings.fix: Love settles from your mid-thirties into a partnership between two people who each run their own lives. Over these years the score between you matters less, and you lean on a partner without feeling smaller.

findings.quote: "and it is when love and money start to move together"
findings.issue: "It is when" is a broken frame.
findings.fix: Your Home Chapter opens in your mid-thirties, and with it love and money start to move together. You build a home in these years with someone who brings an opening into your life, and you stay for as long as the two of you keep heading somewhere together.

findings.quote: "stayed loud for years … and you stayed because"
findings.issue: "stayed" twice in one sentence.
findings.fix: The people you have loved were strong-willed and hard to predict, and they made you earn every point you won. At least one relationship of yours ran loud for years, with fights over plans and whose turn it was, and you stayed because it held your interest.

findings.quote: "you keep testing your partner with argument"
findings.issue: "Your partner" asserts that the reader has one now, where Q10 allows "a partner".
findings.fix: You show love by talking and teasing, and a quiet partner leaves you lonely even in a happy home. Since you feel close only when your mind is met, you keep testing a partner with argument, and some evenings end colder than either of you meant. What you want is praise and honesty in the same person, and you rarely settle for half.

findings.quote: "the job done the way it should be"
findings.issue: "should" is banned on these pages.
findings.fix: You climb at work through trust, the clean record and the job done the proper way. Because being correct matters to you, you follow the rules others bend, and senior people notice. You rise steadily, and you find it hard to take a risk that could mark your record.

findings.quote: "often before you ask for it"
findings.issue: "often" is a banned hedge.
findings.fix: You end up in charge in most places you work, without asking for it. Because pressure has been familiar since your first years, you take on serious work that makes others nervous. You rise through hard roles, and you find easy ones dull within months.

findings.quote: "You keep giving after you can afford to"
findings.issue: It says the opposite of what it means ("after you can no longer afford to").
findings.fix: You give freely in your family, the treat paid for and the loan made without terms. Because an older relative showed you that generosity makes people love you, you find it hard to refuse anyone close. You keep giving past what you can afford, and you resent it only later.

findings.quote: "a clean scoreboard and nobody holding the other end"
findings.issue: A scoreboard has no other end, so the image breaks.
findings.fix: You work best when the task is yours from start to finish and your name is on it. Because your own effort is how you measure yourself, you resent shared credit more than hard work, and you slow down the moment a manager hovers. What you want from a job is a clean scoreboard that counts only you.

findings.quote: "more pleasure than any title … Your work runs on pleasure"
findings.issue: "pleasure" twice in one unit.
findings.fix: You work best on things that feed people in some way, a meal or a lesson or a well-made thing. Because making something well gives you more pleasure than any title, you turn down promotions that would take you away from the work itself. Your work runs on appetite, and you do more of it in a happy month than in a pressured year.

findings.criterion: A1 (a beat fits its ages), D6
findings.quote: D090, ages 1 to 10: "Safety kept you in one place too long during those years, and your duties grew faster than your reward."; D061, ages 4 to 13: "Work came easily in those years"; D144, ages 5 to 14: "Rules and rank pressed on your work during those years"; D190, ages 4 to 13: "Rich food, late nights and easy evenings piled up in those years"; D185, ages 75 to 84: "Your work gains structure in these ten years, a clear role with real responsibility."
findings.issue: The By-decade tab keeps every decade that ends after ten (depthResolve.js line 273, `l.endAge >= DEC_MIN`), while step 2 keeps only decades that start at ten or later (domainsResolve.js line 103, `l.startAge >= DEC_MIN`), so decades lived as a child print adult work and habit lines, and decades past seventy print promotion lines (渊海子平 论年月日时 and 三命通会 论小运: the years to fifteen are read through the year column, the family and the small luck, never through 官禄).

findings.quote: "chosen work that paid by results over work that paid by the hour. You have had big wins and sharp drops"

findings.fix: "Since your late teens you have chosen work where you were measured against the people beside you, by sales or rankings or a shared target. You have won big with partners and lost ground to them, and you have rarely wished for a duller job."

findings.quote: "People who trusted you early have put your name forward … a manager or a mentor … Your references have opened doors for you more than once"
findings.issue: Backers, mentors and references are the Sage's patronage (the Sage's own beat reads "vouched for you or quietly put your name forward"), so the Magistrate beat reads as the Sage and loses rank, rules and the role (子平真诠 论正官: 官 is rank and the order one serves; 论印绶: 印 is protection and support from above).
findings.fix: "Your record has spoken for you at work since your late teens, each role done by the rules and each title kept clean. Promotions have reached you on schedule, and you have rarely had to ask for a step up."

findings.quote: "your record stayed clean … the reputation followed you into later work"
findings.issue: A clean record and a reputation are the Magistrate's (on D052 the Magistrate beat beside it says "saw the clean record"), so the Steward decade loses earned and kept value (子平真诠 论财: 正财 is wealth earned and held by one's own effort; 论正官 holds name and rank).
findings.fix: "Steady work paid you fairly in those years, and you kept most of what you earned. You became known as the person who delivers on time, and that steadiness carried you into later work."

findings.quote: "Since steady practice is what you trust, you are slow to take on work you cannot yet do well, and you miss a few openings that way."
findings.issue: The cost is the Steward's caution, while the Artisan's cost everywhere else in the section is ease ("Ambition softens … the easy option keeps winning"), so the lead reads as the wrong character (三命通会 论食神: 食神 is plenty, enjoyment and ease, and its excess is comfort, not caution).
findings.fix: "Your best work comes from a skill you enjoy, in fields where the hands or the senses know things. Because the work itself is the pleasure, you stay with what you already do well, and you let harder openings pass. You are seldom the loudest on a team, and your work is the work that holds up."

findings.quote: "Your body stays strong on routine." · "a fixed hour to rise and a daily walk or workout" · "From your late forties your health rests on routine … Days with no shape drain your energy and ordered ones bring it back"
findings.issue: Routine, order and a fixed hour are the Magistrate's, so the General reads as rules; on D112 the same character runs on adrenaline at the Month Gate and on routine at the Hour Gate (子平真诠 论偏官: 七杀 is the pressure that bears on the self and has to be met; 论正官: 官 is order kept).
findings.fix: Headline: "Your body stays strong by being tested." Recognition: "You treat your body as something to test, with an early start and a tough workout most days. Because strength is part of how you see yourself, you ignore tiredness until it slows you down. Your energy is at its best when the week asks something hard of you." Ahead: "From your late forties your body answers to the high standard you set it, an early start and a demanding week. You stay fitter than most people your age, and you feel it within days whenever you push on without rest."

findings.quote: "Because ease restores you, you let the ease run on past the point it helps you"
findings.issue: Ease is the Artisan's force; the Sage's is being looked after, which its own ahead beat and seat card say ("the company of people who look after you") (子平真诠 论印绶: 印 shelters and supports the self; 三命通会 论食神: 食神 is enjoyment and ease).
findings.fix: "You stay well on regular meals, unhurried walks and early nights, and you sleep badly the week the rhythm breaks. Because being looked after restores you, you let others carry your pace for longer than it helps, until days with no effort leave you flat and low on energy. You feel best in a week that holds a small challenge."

findings.quote: "Because tension at home reaches your body before you name it, a bad month with a partner shows up in your appetite and your rest."
findings.issue: The mechanism is tension at home, which is the General's Day reading ("Your body carries whatever strain your home holds"), so the Artisan, the Sage and the General give one Health reading at the Day Gate and the Artisan's own appetite and pleasure come last (三命通会 论食神: 食神 is appetite and plenty).
findings.fix: "Your health runs on appetite and ease, and you are at your best in the seasons when meals at home are long and evenings are slow. Because pleasure is how your body recovers, a tense month with a partner shows first in how little you enjoy your food. You get well again through ordinary comfort, a shared meal and an early night."

findings.quote: "both slip the moment it turns tense … a week of bad feeling at home drains your energy before you have named the problem"
findings.issue: The same collapse as DC-013: the Sage's Day lead runs on household tension and echoes the Artisan's "before you name it", where the Sage's force is being cared for (子平真诠 论印绶).
findings.fix: "You sleep well and eat well when someone at home takes care of you, and both slip in the weeks you are left to cope alone. Because being cared for is how your body settles, you get over a hard stretch fastest with a partner close by. You are strongest in the seasons you feel most looked after."

findings.quote: "Because food and rest are pleasures to you, you eat late and sleep short in busy months"
findings.issue: The cause does not produce the effect (enjoying food and rest would protect them), so the reader has to read it twice (三命通会 论食神: the Artisan's enjoyment of food is what keeps the body well).
findings.fix: "Your body and your work move together, and both run best on regular meals and real rest. Because you enjoy your work as much as your food and sleep, busy months push your meals late and your nights short, and your energy drops. You notice tiredness in your work before you feel it, and you put it right with a few good nights."

findings.quote: "Your health has no fixed pattern of its own … the change has no obvious cause", then "In your heaviest thinking seasons you also forget to eat and sleep properly"

You feel well for some stretches of years and worn for others, and you sense each change in your body before you can name its cause."

findings.quote: "You have been asked to lead in hard moments … You turned down at least one easy way out"
findings.issue: On D144 it follows "grown out of hard moments" (qisha_month_stem) and "at least once you turned down an easier job" (qisha_month_branch), so "hard moments", "turned down" and "at least" each print two or three times.
findings.fix: "Since your late forties you have been the one asked to lead, in a crisis or on a committee or in work nobody else would take on. The demanding roles have kept you sharp, and you have stayed in them long after others stepped back."
