Add a qa check that no composed page carries a gap row and a ruling decade in the same gate. Evidence, by kind: 8 pages contradict a decade marked "now" (D007, D019, D021, D087, D092, D110, D128, D142). 7 contradict a decade lived inside the gate (D040, D043, D059, D077, D089, D136, D137).

findings.pages: Text written for later life: D035 (age 34), D089 (32), D007 (35), D137 (23), D138 (23), D142 (21), D202 (37). Hour-led but age-neutral: D077, D128.
findings.quote: D035: "You grow in later life by watching bold people take risks and judging their bets with an experienced eye". D089: "You take up new skills in later life with the same seriousness you brought to your first job". D137: "You see further in later life, and faster." D138: "With each decade you go deeper into rare subjects".
findings.issue: The ruling defines the lead as the highest seat among the gates the reader has reached. When no reached gate holds a seat, the composer falls back to an unreached Hour seat (`opened.length ? opened : seats`, line 82), so a reader of 21 to 37 gets a later-life recognition as "how you are now". Classically the Hour pillar is the late years and the people after you (渊海子平, 论年月日时: 时为子息晚景).
findings.fix: **Rule (owner):** when no reached gate rules the domain, HOW YOU ARE and the headline read either `domain_unruled.{d}` or a new present-tense trait line per Hour seat (how the trait shows before 48). The Hour seat's later-life bloom stays in its ahead beat. If instead the units are rewritten age-neutral, two examples. `jiecai_hour_stem.Growth.recognition`: "You grow by backing bold people and judging their bets. Because a contest keeps you sharp, other people's risks teach you as much as your own, and you lose interest in cautious company. You come alive around anyone daring enough to try something foolish." `bijian_hour_stem.Growth.recognition`: "You take up a new skill with the same seriousness you brought to your first one. Because your own standard is the only one you answer to, you keep raising it long after anyone else is watching. You find it hard to learn beside other people, and you lose some of the help that would come from it." Headlines: "You grow by backing the daring." · "You keep raising your own standard." · "You see further than you can explain." · "Your mind stays quick and restless."

findings.quote: D202, ages 1 to 10: "Unconventional paths taught you most in those years, a strange course, a self-taught skill or a mentor outside the usual." D136, ages 3 to 12: "you came out of it with work that still feels like the most important you have done". D002, ages 2 to 11: "Your progress in those years came from peers who were your equals".
findings.issue: The By decade tab keeps any decade with `endAge >= DEC_MIN`, so decades that start in infancy get lines written for teens and adults. The round-1 fix (M3: "decades read only inside the life window their lines are written for") filters on `startAge >= DEC_MIN` in `resolveDomains` and was lost in the new view. Classical ground: the years before the first luck pillar, and early childhood, are read through 童限 and the Year Pillar, not as an adult decade (三命通会, 论小运 and 童限).
findings.fix: **Rule:** filter byDecade on `l.startAge >= DEC_MIN`, as `resolveDomains` does for the lived decade. Or, if the owner wants early decades shown, add a child-voiced `decade_lines.{d}.{pole}.early` set. 12 rows on 12 of 50 pages.

findings.pages: 枭神夺食: D014, D040, D087, D100, D164 (lifted classically) and D137 (formed). 杀印相生 on Overfueled charts: D048, D068, D089, D113, D138, D150, D050, D149. 伤官配印 on Overfueled charts: D131, D178.
findings.quote: "You also think so long about a thing that you miss the moment to make it, and you keep a drawer of nearly finished work."
findings.issue: The pairs fire on presence alone (03_RULINGS step 1), but the classical pairing forms only under conditions, and the texts assert the formed version. 枭神夺食 harms only where the Artisan is the useful god, which means a strong self. A wealth star restrains the Alchemist and lifts it (子平真诠 论食神 and 论印绶; 渊海子平, 偏印 倒食, 偏财可解). Of the 6 charts in this group, 4 are Underfueled, where the Alchemist is wanted and the Artisan is a drain (D014, D040, D100, D164). 4 also carry a wealth star (D040 正财; D087 偏财 ×2; D100 正财, 偏财, 正财; D164 偏财 ×2). Only D137 meets both conditions. On D014 and D040 the Alchemist's own decades read as helping, so the page calls one force a gift and a thief at once. 杀印相生 and 伤官配印 are the weak-self pairings (子平真诠 论偏官: 杀用印 wants 印 and 身旺 luck; 滴天髓: 杀重身轻，化之以印; 子平真诠 论伤官: 伤官用印 "反要伤官旺，身稍弱，始为秀气"). Here 8 of 13 and 2 of 5 fire on Overfueled charts.
findings.fix: **Owner ruling needed** (the presence trigger is ruled, so this is not changed here). Option A: add the conditions. 枭神夺食 fires only on an Overfueled chart with no 偏财 or 正财 seated. 杀印相生 and 伤官配印 fire only where the 印 is a catalyst, otherwise a variant line. Option B: keep the trigger and rewrite each line to hold for every chart with both sides. For example, `xiao_shen_duo_shi.Mind`: "You also weigh a thing longer than most people before you make it, and the thinking and the making pull against each other in you." Same class of defect as STATE M-1 (a rule that ignores what the chart already holds).

findings.quote: "Your four gates have all opened, so your growth moves with your decades from here."
findings.issue: The note fires only when no current or coming decade rules the domain (`!future.length`). It points the reader to decades exactly when the page has none ahead: on all 7 pages the By decade tab is lived only. Classical ground: a decade rules a domain only through its character (三命通会, 论大运).
findings.fix: Rewrite the string: "Your four gates have all opened, and no decade ahead rules {own}, so the pattern above is the one it keeps." This follows the shape of the Love note.

findings.pages: Growth.day: D002, D012, D019, D025, D202. Mind.day: D007, D014, D021.
findings.quote: "you have started fewer new things than in any years before". "reading and study have had less of your week than they once did".
findings.issue: Both Day-gate gap rows assert a measured decline that an empty gate cannot show. They fire in the reader's first year of the gate, where "since your mid-thirties" covers months: 7 of the 8 pages are age 35, and with M-6 two of them (D021, D025, born in November) are still 34. "Than in any years before" is also awkward. Classical ground: a reading proceeds from what the chart holds, and an empty seat is silent, not a loss (子平真诠, 论用神).
findings.fix: Growth.day: "Since your mid-thirties your growth has come through the life you already have, the work and the home, more than through new starts." Mind.day: "Since your mid-thirties your thinking has gone into the work and the home in front of you, more than into study for its own sake." Also show no gap row in the year the reader enters the gate (age = gate start).

findings.quote: "you stayed in most of them a little past the point they could teach you"
findings.issue: The lived beat repeats the recognition's cost on the same page ("you wait longer than you need to"). It also borrows the Sage's cost, word for word ("past the point they teach you anything", `zhengyin_month_branch.Growth.recognition`). The Magistrate reads as duty and rank (子平真诠 论正官), not as shelter.
findings.fix: "You grew through formal steps from your late teens on, a qualification finished or a rank reached or a role handed to you. Each structure you joined gave you a clear duty and a clear measure, and you grew most in the years you were trusted with more."

findings.quote: "You have stayed somewhere safe for longer than it served you at least once"
findings.issue: This repeats the recognition beside it ("you stay in comfortable roles past the point they teach you anything"). On D083 the Sage's seat card says it a third time.
findings.fix: "From your late teens you have grown in steady steps, each one taken only after you felt well prepared. The people who taught you in those years gave you a base you still stand on, and you did better than you feared each time you moved."

findings.quote: "you came to know your field better than you let on, and you have rarely made a show of it"
findings.issue: This restates both recognitions it sits under: "You know far more than you claim to" (D085) and "You underrate your own knowledge more than anyone around you does" (D095).
findings.fix: "From your late teens you took in courses, books and advice from people who knew more, and kept nearly all of it. Over those years you learned fastest from the ones who trusted you early, and you still go back to what they taught you."

findings.quote: "Because books and patient adults were part of your childhood, you learn easily inside a course or a school"
findings.issue: One idea three times on one page. The recognition tells the childhood that the lived beat tells ("As a child you had books at home and adults who answered your questions"), and it says the school frame that the pair line says ("you learn well inside a frame like a school"). The cause is biography where the house wants the reader's need.
findings.fix: "You approach a new subject expecting to be taught well, and you go looking for the best teacher before you open a book. Because a guide makes learning feel safe to you, you value a qualification for its own sake. You find it harder to learn where nobody is showing you the way."

findings.quote: "people notice the answer before they understand the route"
findings.issue: This repeats the lived beat directly below it ("reaching the right answer by a route nobody had taught"), and the close leans on the watcher ("the first thing people remember about you").
findings.fix: "You come at problems from an unexpected direction, and the strange angle is the one you trust. Because your mind took its own path from the start, the obvious approach bores you before you have tried it. Your way of thinking is the first thing people notice about you, and you have stopped hiding it."

findings.quote: "Younger people come to rely on your judgement in these years"
findings.issue: Two Sage Hour beats in a row open "Younger people" and say the same thing: the young consult you. The lived twin of this seat ("talks with people you trust") already points inward.
findings.fix: "Reading fills more of your days from your late forties, and you remember more of it than you did in your busiest years. Talks with the few people you trust keep your thinking clear in these years, and you give your judgement carefully when it is asked for."

findings.quote: "quick to spot the flaw and slow to explain it"
findings.issue: Spotting the flaw is the Virtuoso's act (its year line, its month seats and its seat cards all find flaws). On D021 this Alchemist beat sits directly above the Virtuoso's "Your mind has gone looking for faults". The Alchemist is odd, private knowledge (三命通会 论偏印) and the Virtuoso is the critic (论伤官).
findings.fix: "Your thinking has set you apart at work since your late teens, quick to reach an odd answer and slow to explain it. You have left more than one project half finished because the interesting part was solved, and the finishing bored you."

findings.pages: D128, D191 (and D110 for the ahead beat)
findings.quote: "You grow fastest when the task is new to you, a different kind of audience or a skill nobody expects you to take up." "taking up a new field or a new way of working". "You grow for as long as the work stays new."
findings.issue: The Virtuoso reads as the Horizon: novelty, a new field, work nobody expected. That is nearly the Horizon's own lived beat ("a skill or a trade or a kind of work nobody expected from you"). Its own ahead beat ("Saying out loud what you used to keep to yourself") is about the voice, so lived and ahead disagree. Classical ground: 伤官 is talent that defies the rule (子平真诠 论伤官); range and new ventures are 偏财.
findings.fix: Recognition: "You grow where someone has said a thing cannot be done, a rule to test or a method to beat. Because being told how bores you before it tires you, you leave a settled position sooner than others think wise. Each break costs you some comfort, and you speak more plainly after every one." Headline: "You grow by breaking the rule you were given." Lived: "Past your late forties you have said out loud more than once what others in the room would not, and changed your way of working because of it. Each break looked risky to the people around you, and you grew more for it than in the calmer years before."

findings.quote: "you came out of it with work that still feels like the most important you have done"
findings.issue: A heavy decade must name its cost and what carried the reader. This one reads as the best decade of the reader's life and reads better than the helping line. It also repeats "few people around you shared", which the Alchemist's year line and month beat echo ("people around you" three times on D178). Classical ground: a decade bringing the unwanted god is a burden (子平真诠, 论行运).
findings.fix: "You turned inward in those years, into subjects nobody near you could follow. The long stretches alone left you out of step with the people close to you, and what carried you was one piece of work you still count among your best."

findings.quote: "Underneath, you grow most through the years that weigh on you, and you have left every heavy stretch more skilled than you entered it."
findings.issue: The line says only the General's half. 杀印相生 is the Sage turning pressure into support (子平真诠 论偏官, 杀用印; 滴天髓, 化之以印). So on General-led pages the line restates the lead and makes no counterweight. On D048 "left you more capable" or "more skilled" appears three times (General lived, this line, General decade).
findings.fix: "Underneath, the years that weigh on you send you toward the study and the people who steady you, and you have ended every heavy stretch more sure of who you are."

findings.quote: "In you this works fast, and you learn from pressure in the same week it arrives."
findings.issue: Sharing a pillar makes a pairing close and strong (有情, 子平真诠). It says nothing about speed. The speed claim contradicts the golden Alchemist leads it follows ("You grow in long quiet stretches that look like standing still", D048 and D113; "you rework a problem long after others have moved on", D050).
findings.fix: "In you the two sit at one gate, and you rarely meet a pressure without learning from it."

findings.quote: "more than one ended only when you finally learned from someone better"
findings.issue: The Twin grows beside an equal (三命通会 论比肩), and its own recognition and seat card say "beside you" and "one trusted colleague". Learning from someone better is the Sage.
findings.fix: "Long flat stretches have marked your learning since your late teens, and more than one ended only when you finally worked beside an equal. You remember each of those people, and you owe them more thanks than you have given."

findings.quote: "You see the pattern before others have finished explaining it"
findings.issue: This nearly copies the Alchemist's opener ("You see the shape of a problem before anyone has finished describing it to you", `pianyin_hour_stem.Mind.recognition`), so two characters open as one force. The Virtuoso's mark is the sharp objection (子平真诠 论伤官).
findings.fix: "You spot the weak step in an argument at once, and boredom reaches you long before the lesson ends. Since your thinking was praised early for speed, you are careless with the slower parts of a problem. Your mind does its best work on hard problems with someone watching, and you drift when it has neither."

findings.quote: "often away from what was expected of you"
findings.issue: "often" is a banned hedge.
findings.fix: "You grew in those years by going your own way, away from what was expected of you. The progress was real and nearly invisible, and you kept going on your own conviction while you felt behind."

findings.quote: "the people around you often underrate where you are"
findings.issue: "often" is a banned hedge.
findings.fix: "You grow in long quiet stretches that look like standing still, and then you change all at once. Because you change on the inside first, the people around you underrate where you are, and you let them. You are further along than anyone watching would guess."

findings.quote: "it is often the thing that matters most"
findings.issue: "often" is a banned hedge.
findings.fix: "You think best alone, on problems other people have given up on or never noticed. Because you trust only the conclusions you reached alone, you rework a problem long after others have moved on, and you find small talk harder than hard questions. You keep most of what you know to yourself, and it is the thing that matters most."

findings.quote: "Even so, you learn well inside a frame"
findings.issue: "Even so" leans on a contrast the keyed unit cannot know. After the three leads it follows ("harder to learn where nobody is guiding you"; "You know far more than you claim to"; "one good question in front of you"), it turns on nothing.
findings.fix: "You also learn well inside a frame like a school or a discipline, and you keep studying long after the course has ended."

findings.criterion: A1 (Q10, a claim the chart cannot know)
findings.quote: "You give your partner your best ideas first"
findings.issue: "Your partner" presumes the reader has one now. Q10 rules "a partner" at the Day Gate.
findings.fix: "You think best out loud, with one person close enough to hear the rough version and sharp enough to push back. Because your ideas only feel real once they have been tested on someone, an evening of silence at home leaves you restless. You give a partner your best ideas first, and your harshest opinions too."

findings.quote: "Your clearest thinking so far has happened alone"
findings.issue: "So far" fits a reader inside the Day Gate. The same beat is shown to readers past 48 (here 67), for whom the gate (渊海子平: 日柱, the middle years and the partner) has closed.
findings.fix: "Your clearest thinking has happened alone, late at night or on long walks, away from the people you live with. More than once you have surprised a partner with a decision you had been weighing for weeks in silence."

findings.quote: "Your clearest thinking so far has happened in long talks with someone close"
findings.issue: The same "so far" slip, shown at 68.
findings.fix: "Your clearest thinking has happened in long talks with someone close, more than in study or alone at a desk. You have changed your mind more than once because a partner disagreed, and you have also argued long after either of you was listening."

findings.criterion: A1 (contradicts the seat card beside it)
findings.quote: "a written method or a body of work"
findings.issue: The seat card beside it closes "your method stays unwritten for longer than it should".
findings.fix: "You grow from your late forties by mastering one rare thing completely. You put what you learn into a form others can use, a method or a body of work, and you see it travel further than you do."

findings.quote: "you end up with a character that others hold up as an example"
findings.issue: "A character" clashes with the house term for the ten (the characters), on a page that names them.
findings.fix: "Past your late forties you keep improving at what you already know, and each year adds polish more than novelty. You grow wiser through repetition and care, and you become the example others hold up."

findings.quote: "Since your late forties people and daily life"
findings.issue: Without a comma it first reads "your late forties people".
findings.fix: "Since your late forties, people and daily life have held more of your thinking than ideas, and you have turned your curiosity to practical things."

findings.quote: "explaining things you once took for granted since your late forties"
findings.issue: The time phrase attaches to "took for granted", so the sentence reads twice.
findings.fix: "Since your late forties you have found yourself explaining things you once took for granted, and it has taught you as much as it taught others. You have written down or passed on more of what you know than in all the years before."

findings.quote: "Your thinking sharpens against received ideas this year"
findings.issue: "Received ideas" is C1 to C2 idiom.
findings.fix: "Your thinking sharpens against the ideas you are handed this year, and you find flaws in what others accept faster than you can keep them to yourself."

findings.quote: "you would not trade them back"
findings.issue: "Trade back" means to return a trade. The idiom is "would not trade one".
findings.fix: "From your late teens your mind went its own way, into a subject or a method most people around you did not follow. You have spent more nights with a question than with company, and you would not trade one of them."

findings.quote: "One seat rules Growth in your chart. One sits in your Late Chapter." "Two seats rule Mind in your chart. Two sit in your Rising Chapter."
findings.issue: When every seat is in one chapter, the second sentence repeats the count.
findings.fix: One seat: "One seat rules {domain} in your chart. It sits in your {chapter}." All seats in one chapter: "{N} seats rule {domain} in your chart. Both sit in your {chapter}." (for three or more: "All {n} sit in your {chapter}.")

findings.quote: "You grow fastest when life is hard"
findings.issue: On D043 this opener meets the owner-approved General year line, "You grow fastest this year where something forces you to". (D019, D128 and D191 have the same clash; D128 and D191 go with DD-014. D019's pair is two approved units, so it is the owner's call.)
findings.fix: "You grow when life is hard, and you lose direction when it gets too comfortable. Because difficulty was where you first found your strength, you sign up for the harder option by choice, and a year with nothing hard in it leaves you restless. You have done your best learning in seasons other people would call their worst."

findings.quote: D029 "you say the sharp thing in company and lose a friend or two to it" then "More than once a friendship ended over something you said in public"; D076 "you lose the friend along with the money" then "you still count the friend as a loss more than the money"; D139 "You know the difference between the two" then "you knew which were which"; D079 "colleagues who stood with you when the work was hard" then "the people you worked hardest beside"
findings.issue: The lead seat is always one of the page's seats, and its How you are and its lived beat name the same drive and the same cost, so steps 1 and 2 say one thing twice on most pages.
findings.fix: Rule: a seat's recognition says how the drive works now (its cause and present cost); its lived beat says what the gate's age span built (who came into the circle, what it kept or cost, tied to the span), and the two share no mechanism and no three-word run (add to the gate). Rewrite the ten lived beats listed; the recognitions are the stronger units and stay. DE-008 and DE-024 are two of the ten.

findings.pages: 27 of 70 units, on every page; D145 7 of its 14 units, D039 6 of 12, D115 5 of 12, D029 4 of 7
findings.quote: General "you kept the ones who stayed"; Virtuoso "you have kept every friend who stayed through it"; Rival "you have kept the rival who took a loss well"; Twin "One steady friend carries you through the decade"; Rival "What carries you is one friend who never competes with you"; Horizon "One old friend who stayed kept you steady"; Magistrate "you found ease with one friend outside that circle"
findings.issue: Six characters close on one figure, the few who stayed, so in Social the Twin, Rival, Virtuoso, Horizon, Magistrate and General read as one force and a page repeats the close up to seven times (source: 滴天髓 性情, each of the ten keeps its own disposition).
findings.fix: Rule: a Social close and a heavy decade's carry-through come from the character's own force. Twin: standing on your own. Rival: a fair contest or a share given. Virtuoso: the people who want the sharp voice. Horizon: a new door. Magistrate: a role that gives standing. General: a test passed together. Artisan: ease and the table. Alchemist: one private understanding. Sage: being taken in. Page budget: one "kept the ones who stayed / one friend" close per page, counted by the compound check. Rewrite the 27 units in the polish round (DE-012 is the first).

findings.pages: D003 (Twin, ages 2 to 11), D039 (Twin, 4 to 13), D076 (Horizon, 1 to 10), D121 (Twin, 1 to 10), D139 (Magistrate, 4 to 13), D145 (Magistrate, 5 to 14), D183 (Twin, 5 to 14): 7 of 25
findings.quote: D076, ages 1 to 10: "Your circle spread wide in those years, through travel, work and friends of friends"; D121, ages 1 to 10: "sure that few people matched your standard"; D183, 5 to 14: "you held yourself apart from most groups"
findings.issue: The By decade tab keeps any decade that ends at 10 or later, so a decade that opens in infancy is read with a lived line written for an adult, and a toddler's years name work, travel and standards (source: 渊海子平 reads a child's years by the 小儿 rules, upbringing and 关煞, not by standing and work; 三命通会 论大运 dates a decade from its start age, which the line must fit).
findings.fix: Rule (resolver): `resolveDomainView.byDecade` reads a lived decade only when `l.startAge >= DEC_MIN`, as `resolveDomains` already does for its last past decade (`depthResolve.js` line 273, `l.endAge >= DEC_MIN` becomes `l.startAge >= DEC_MIN`). If the owner wants those decades shown, add a child tense per god, domain and pole instead (10 Social units, 60 across the eight domains).

findings.quote: "in these years" or "in those years" in every decade line; last sentences "…, and you lean on that friend often", "…, and you value that friend more than a full calendar", "…, and you return to them again and again"
findings.issue: The label already carries the decade's years, yet nearly every decade line names "these years" again and 52 of 70 units end on the same ", and you …" joint, so a page of four decades reads as one frame four times (D003: "and you" ×17, D183 ×19).
findings.fix: Rule: a decade line does not name its period (the label does), and the domain parts of one page end on ", and you" at most three times (compound check). Apply in the polish round with DE-002, since the same units are rewritten.

findings.quote: "Your closest friends are the ones you and a partner both respect, other couples and old friends who treat your home as a unit." · headline "Your friends are shared, few and loyal."
findings.issue: The Day Gate counts as reached at every age, so a reader of 33 is told they already live in a couple's circle, and the same seat's ahead beat then says that circle begins in the mid-thirties (source: 渊海子平, the day branch is the partner's seat; the gate, 35 to 47, says when).
findings.fix: Recognition: "Your closest friends are the few you would let into your home, people who stand level with you. Because respect is what keeps you close to anyone, you let wider acquaintances fade without a word. You keep a small circle, and you can say why each person in it is there." (51 words). Headline: "Your friends are few, level and loyal."

findings.pages: D099, D139 (unit also on D071, D127, D141)
findings.quote: "your circle has stayed smaller than the people around you expected"
findings.issue: Keyed by gate only, the gap row asserts a small circle, which the Year seat on the same page denies: D099 "Your friends are many and loyal", D139 "You make friends fast" (source: 子平真诠 论宫分用神配六亲, an empty gate says only that it holds no seat and cancels nothing another gate holds).
findings.fix: "Since sixteen your study, work and family have come before your friendships, and you have seen friends around the edges of a full week." (24 words)

findings.quote: "Since your mid-thirties your evenings have gone to home and work more than to friends, and you have watched your circle thin without anyone deciding it."
findings.issue: Shown to readers who have just turned 35, it reports a thinning already watched, and it is a loss with nothing that carries the reader through (source: 三命通会 根苗花实, the Day pillar's years open at the gate, so the line must hold from its first year).
findings.fix: "From your mid-thirties home and work take the evenings that friends used to have, and you meet your circle by plan more than by chance." (25 words)

findings.quote: "Friends and colleagues have brought you their crises since your late teens, and several of your closest friendships began with someone else's bad news."
findings.issue: The Sage is the force that shelters and teaches the reader, but both Social units make the reader the shelter for others, so the character is turned inside out and the lived beat repeats How you are (source: 子平真诠 论印绶, 印 is what 生身, the protector of the self; 三命通会 论印绶, 印 主 长上 庇荫).
findings.fix: "Since your late teens your closest friendships have grown out of being taken in, an older colleague who taught you or a friend's family who made room for you. You still ask those people first when you need advice, and you learned from them how to listen." (47 words). The recognition stays, so the page shows shelter received and then given.

findings.quote: "As a child you were popular with other children and with adults, and you were invited to more than your share. By the time you were grown"
findings.issue: The Rival's child beat is the Artisan's (popularity, invitations) with no contest or share in it, and "By the time you were grown" runs past the Year Gate's fifteen (source: 三命通会 and 渊海子平 on 比劫, 劫财 主 争夺 and 分财; 食神 is appetite and ease; 三命通会 根苗花实, the Year pillar holds the years to fifteen).
findings.fix: "As a child you shared what you had and competed for what you wanted, and other children gathered round you. By your teens you had a wide circle and one or two close friends who mattered far more, and you knew which were which." (44 words)

findings.quote: "You have lost a real friend at least once by treating them as a contact."
findings.issue: The close is a charge on how the reader treated a friend, and a single undated event that How you are cannot know (Q9 allows past patterns only).
findings.fix: Built on DE-019: "You collect contacts the way other people collect friends, and you love introducing people who will get on. Because your network brings you work and money, the useful friendships and the warm ones get mixed together. You give a real friend the same quick hour you give a contact, and you are the last to notice the difference." (58 words)

findings.quote: "When one of those plans fails, you lose the friend along with the money."
findings.issue: How you are closes on a predicted loss of a friend and of money, the outcome close BIZ_04 rules too harsh, and the lived beat beside it says the same (DE-001). The Rival's shared money is classical (三命通会 论比劫) and stays.
findings.fix: "Your friends and colleagues are mostly the same people, and you go into business with the ones you like. Because you trust the people you enjoy, you agree to shared plans before the terms are clear. You mix friendship and money without a line between them, and you are slow to ask which one a deal is really about." (59 words)

findings.pages: D049, D071, D076, D115, D123, D139 (both decades on one page); unit also on D079, D084
findings.quote: "One steady friend carries you through the decade, and you value that friend more than a full calendar."
findings.issue: On six pages the heavy Twin and heavy Rival decades sit side by side and both carry the reader with one friend ("What carries you is one friend who never competes with you"), and the Twin's carry is not the Twin's own force (source: 渊海子平 论比肩, the Twin is the self's own strength).
findings.fix: "Company that truly matches you is scarce in these years, and crowded groups wear you out quickly. Standing on your own carries you through the decade, and you value a quiet evening more than a full calendar." (37 words)

findings.quote: "the people who like it like it a great deal"
findings.issue: "like it like it" makes the reader parse the sentence twice, and the clause adds nothing the next sentence does not say.
findings.fix: "You become more outspoken in these years, and the people who enjoy a sharp voice seek you out. You gather an audience of your own, and you lose patience with company that asks you to be quieter." (37 words)

findings.quote: "You are the person people ask to chair the meeting or hold the keys or settle the dispute."
findings.issue: No Social seat's gate has opened at 22, so the resolver falls back to the unopened Hour seat and tells the reader now what the Hour Gate holds from 48, while the seat card beside it says "in later life" (source: 三命通会 根苗花实, the Hour pillar is the 实, the late years).
findings.fix: Rule (resolver): when no seat's gate has opened, How you are reads `TEMPLATED tpl_domains · domain_unruled.Social` (or the current decade's line) and the Hour seat speaks only in its ahead beat; the headline still comes from the Hour seat. In `domainsResolve.js` the lead becomes the first opened seat or none.

findings.quote: "you decide more than anyone credits you for"
findings.issue: Broken idiom (one credits a person with a thing, or gives credit for it).
findings.fix: "You are the one who keeps a group working, the colleague who remembers the deadline and the friend who makes the plan happen. Because order calms you, you take on the organising without being asked, and people come to depend on it. Your place in a circle is quiet, and you decide more than anyone gives you credit for."

findings.quote: "Friends you had no shared task with drifted further"
findings.issue: A comparative with nothing to compare.
findings.fix: "Your friendships have grown out of work and shared duties since your late teens, the colleagues you trusted and the seniors who trusted you. Friends you had no shared task with drifted away, and you kept the ones bound to you by a duty for years after the job ended."

findings.quote: "often with one friend who mirrors you like a sibling"
findings.issue: "often" is a banned hedge.
findings.fix: "Your friendships since your late teens have been between equals, with one friend in particular who mirrors you like a sibling. More than once you have lent money or time to a friend and found it harder to talk about than the friendship could bear."

findings.quote: "you lean on that friend often"
findings.issue: "often" is a banned hedge.
findings.fix: "Comparison runs through your friendships in these years, and you notice who earns more and who wins more. What carries you is one friend who never competes with you, and you lean on that friend above all others."

findings.quote: "people who should meet"
findings.issue: "should" is banned on the domain pages.
findings.fix: "You collect contacts the way other people collect friends, and you love introducing people who will get on. Because your network brings you work and money, the useful friendships and the warm ones get mixed together. You have lost a real friend at least once by treating them as a contact." (DE-010 then rewrites the close.)

findings.quote: "You got through on the company itself"
findings.issue: Broken idiom.
findings.fix: "Friendship and contest mixed in those years, and more than once a friend took credit or a prize you had earned. The company itself got you through, and you learned to tell an ally from a competitor."

findings.quote: "As a child your remarks were the ones repeated"
findings.issue: Dangling modifier ("As a child" attaches to "your remarks").
findings.fix: "When you were a child, your remarks were the ones repeated at family gatherings and in class. By your teens you had a few friends who loved your wit and a teacher or two who had given up on you."

findings.quote: "Other children took a while to warm to you as a child, because you stood at the edge of groups for a long time first."
findings.issue: "as a child" repeats "Other children", and "for a long time first" is broken.
findings.fix: "Other children took a while to warm to you, because you stood at the edge of each group for a long time before you joined it. By your teens you had one or two close friends who understood you, and they were enough for you."

findings.quote: "At least once that role cost you a weekend"
findings.issue: A single event where Q9 allows only a pattern tied to the span.
findings.fix: "From your late teens you have been the dependable one in every group, the friend who organised and the colleague who covered. More than once that role cost you a weekend or a holiday you had planned for yourself, and you gave it up without complaint."

findings.quote: "At least one friendship of yours ended over a shared venture, and you still count the friend as a loss more than the money."
findings.issue: A garbled comparison, and a single event where Q9 allows a pattern.
findings.fix: "Your closest friends since your late teens have also been the people you worked or did deals with. More than one friendship of yours has ended over a shared venture, and you still count each friend as a bigger loss than the money."

findings.criterion: A4 (reader the subject of the last sentence)
findings.quote: "and the one or two friends who stayed were enough to carry you"
findings.issue: The last sentence has the circle and the friends as its subjects, not the reader.
findings.fix: "During those years you held yourself apart from most groups, sure that few people matched your standard. Your circle grew smaller than it had been, and you found the one or two friends who stayed were enough to carry you."

findings.quote: "Propriety ruled your social life"
findings.issue: "Propriety" is above the B1–B2 band.
findings.fix: "What was proper ruled your social life in those years, and you kept company with people you were expected to know. You were respected and a little lonely, and you found ease with one friend outside that circle."

findings.quote: "You widen your circle in these years, through travel and new groups and people met through other people."
findings.issue: "through … through" and "people … people" in one sentence.
findings.fix: "You widen your circle in these years, through travel and new groups and the people they lead you to. You make more new friends in this decade than in the one before it."

findings.quote: "Your circle widens this year through chance meetings and friends of friends"
findings.issue: Repeats "friends of friends" from the Horizon helping lived decade on D076, D115 and D183.
findings.fix: "Your circle widens this year through chance meetings and introductions, and you move easily between groups that never meet each other."

findings.quote: "Competition runs through your circle this year over the same invitations and attention"
findings.issue: "Competition … over" takes the wrong preposition (competition is for a thing). Its "runs through" frame also meets the Rival heavy decade's "Comparison runs through your friendships" on D076, D115 and D200, which DE-004's polish round takes, since a tweak keeps the opening.
findings.fix: "Competition runs through your circle this year for the same invitations and attention, and you share your friends more widely than you planned."

findings.quote: "Roles and expectations shape your friendships this year"
findings.issue: Repeats the Magistrate heavy decade's "Duty shapes your friendships" on D011, D024, D029, D039, D099 and D127.
findings.fix: "Roles and expectations mark your friendships this year, a committee seat or a host's duty, and you are known for showing up when you said you would."

findings.quote: "Friends meet you as equals this year"
findings.issue: "equals" already carries the Twin's seat and decade lines on the same pages (five times on D145 and on D199).
findings.fix: "Friends meet you as peers this year, and you spend more time with people who do what you do than with those who look up to you."

findings.quote: "children who competed with you and stood up for you in turn"
findings.issue: Competition is the Rival's force, and on D024, D145 and D199 the Rival decade beside it says "friends who competed with you" (source: 渊海子平 论比肩, the Twin is the peer who stands level; 争夺 belongs to 劫财).
findings.fix: "The friends you made as a child were your equals, children who kept pace with you and stood up for you in turn. The friendships that lasted into your teens were the level ones, and you let the rest go without a fuss."

findings.quote: "You were at your best among a crowd of equals"
findings.issue: "equals" is the Twin's word in the Rival's decade (source: 三命通会 论比劫, 劫财 is the rival who takes a share).
findings.fix: "Those years filled your life with lively company, friends who competed with you and pushed you on. You were at your best among a crowd of rivals, and you won their respect openly."

findings.quote: "the people who shape your next twenty years"
findings.issue: The Day Gate spans 35 to 47, so twenty years runs into the Hour Gate, which holds its own seats (source: 三命通会 根苗花实, the Day pillar is the 花, the middle years).
findings.fix: "Your circle widens from your mid-thirties through a partner's world, through their friends and their family and their work. You will meet the people who shape these years through someone you share a home with."

findings.quote: "One seat rules Social in your chart. One sits in your Rising Chapter."
findings.issue: "One … One" reads as two seats.
findings.fix: For one seat: "One seat rules {domain} in your chart. It sits in your {chapter}."

findings.quote: "The Twin inside the Day Gate · Home Chapter · from 35 · 2027 · inside · coming"
findings.issue: The view word repeats "inside" from the seat's name.
findings.fix: For a branch seat drop the view word: "{seat} inside the {gate} · {chapter} · {span, or from age · year} · {tense}", e.g. "The Twin inside the Day Gate · Home Chapter · from 35 · 2027 · coming".
